adaptations.withheld: sacred or restricted dance: no teaching adaptations

movement_profile.arms_and_hands: Intricate finger and hand gestures performed continuously
movement_profile.footwork: Continuous circular movements, slow and deliberate
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Performed in pairs or circular groups depending on variant
movement_profile.hips_and_torso: Incorporates bending backward with face toward the floor
movement_profile.levels_and_jumps: No jumps described; focus on controlled bending and hand movements
movement_profile.partnering: Historically two men danced together; Perak variant by palace maids without partnering
movement_profile.posture: Upright with controlled body bending backward during acrobatic moves

signature_moves.description: Dancer bends body backward while facing the floor
signature_moves.name: Bending

movement_profile.tempo_feel: Slow to moderate tempo matching ceremonial music
movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Avoid performing outside designated ceremonial occasions or by unauthorized persons

music_profile.musical_form: Includes three songs: Temang Welo, Selong, Mak Inang
music_profile.sound_description: The music features traditional Malay percussion instruments with rhythmic drum beats and melodic gong and flute lines, creating a formal and ceremonial atmosphere.

basic_steps: Begin with standing in a circular formation
Execute intricate finger and hand gestures
Incorporate bending backward movements with face toward the floor
Maintain slow, controlled tempo matching ceremonial music
teaching.formation: Circular or paired (historically two men), or group in garden setting for Perak variant
teaching.level_notes: Beginners start with basic hand gestures and slow circular footwork; advanced dancers incorporate bending and acrobatic elements.
teaching.rhythm: Rhythmic and ceremonial, matching Gendang Terinai songs
